notes:
CRM notes (shorthand):
- Primary contact: CTO Elena Morales; CISO: Rajiv Banerjee.
- Business problem: embed LLM into customer support chat and fraud detection pipelines; need deterministic throughput for peak trading hours.
- Current infra: mix of public cloud (GCP us-west) + 2 on-prem colo sites for sensitive workloads. Strong preference to keep PII models on-prem or in dedicated VPC with strict egress controls.
- Sizing workshop highlights (03/04): collected baseline QPS for three endpoints: chat (steady 80 qps, peak bursts 320 qps), embeddings (20 qps steady, spiky during batch jobs up to 140 qps), reranking (15 qps steady with 4x burst). Token profile: chat avg 120 tokens/request, peak path with long contexts up to 2k tokens for escalations; embeddings 1k tokens per document on batch runs.
- Latency SLOs: conversational UI target p95 < 200ms for generate-lite paths, p95 < 300ms for long-context generation; reranker target p95 < 150ms. Business is sensitive to tail latency during market opens.
- Throughput guarantees ask: sustained token/sec budget ~60k tokens/sec across cluster during daytime peak. Peak burst headroom requested +2x sustained.
- GPU planning notes: recommended baseline of 12x A10G-equivalent GPUs for steady-state with autoscale buffer to 30 GPUs for peak bursts (quantized Llama-variant inference). Discussed mixing higher-memory GPUs for long-context paths.
- Routing/fallback: want automatic fallback to smaller, cheaper model variant (same API surface) when reserved capacity is saturated; prefer policy-based routing by route and cost tier.
- Caching: strong interest in prefix/KV cache for repetitive chat flows (top 15 intents account for 42% of tokens) to cut token/sec by ~28%. Redwood Optimize recommendations requested.
- Security: will require SSO (SAML), customer-managed KMS, audit logs forwarded to Splunk, and monthly export of usage. Data residency: EU-only for some EU customer subset (future phase).
- POC plan: 4-week POC on Dedicated with canary routing of 10% traffic, run two load windows (steady and simulated market open burst). Deliver workshop report with recommended GPU count, latency projections, expected unit cost, and a fallover policy.
- Procurement: finance wants line-item ARR by product (Dedicated + Private option) and SLA penalties clarified for p95 latency misses.
- Quotes from CISO: "Need hard SLAs on tail latency; outages cost us market customers."
- Next steps (short): deliver sizing workbook + quotes (by 2026-03-15), schedule follow-up tech deep-dive on on-prem packaging, sync procurement week of 2026-03-22.
- Open questions: exact on-prem hardware spec allowed; acceptable SLA penalty thresholds; whether encryption-in-use (HSM) required for model weights on-prem.
